topic: Can we achieve a situation where essentially every material can be recycled and reused?
conclusion: Near-universal circularity is plausible as a governed portfolio of designed product systems, but literal repeated recovery of every object is not a meaningful or safe engineering target. The correct comparison is quality-adjusted future service under realistic contamination, routing, market, social-cost, and regional infrastructure conditions.
key_testable_claims: Technical processability exceeds product-grade recovery under realistic contamination and quality requirements.
Design-for-recovery can improve quality-adjusted yield in at least one product class without service failure.
Quality-aware routing can outperform tonnage-maximizing routing in future service or social burden.
Reuse has a product- and region-specific cycle threshold.
External costs change selected private-cost route rankings.
No single route dominates all product classes and regions.
